Jett uses Lightweaver’s Assault to clear Aella and Ghosts of Pendragon, then spends another Assault against a later Aella. Zero keeps rebuilding. Jett’s last draws are low-impact allies rather than Slice and Dice, and he concedes with lethal damage on Zero’s board.

games.summary: Jett wins — Turbo Charge off the top and a Slice and Dice swing tie the final at 1-1

beats.text: Jett finds Turbo Charge after Backup Charger, then establishes Stifling Gyre naming Ghosts of Pendragon. He returns Sadi and uses Incapacitate to stop Zero’s Escape the Wreckage.

The second takes that Assault and Slice and Dice after an Incapacitate exchange. Jett then draws Dungeon Guide from Blinding Orb, reaches level three, and uses the Guide to remove Zero’s Windmill Engineer.

Revealing Luxem Sight recovers three, and the Assault clears the immediate threat. Zero uses Ascension to reset Clarent instead of revealing Jett’s memory again.

Zero uses Imperious Galebind on Jett’s weapons, and Jett activates Poisoned Dagger in response. Clarent prevents the initial damage, but the damage bonus remains. Jett draws Turbo Charge first, then plays Luxem Sight to draw Slice and Dice. The prepared attack followed by Lightweaver’s Assault closes game three.

games.summary: Zero wins — Prismatic Edge removes Jett’s Luxem cards, and Retribution forces a fifth game

beats.text: Zero uses Turbo Charge and Fluffy Shopkeep to prepare a fast level-up. Jett takes an aggressive early Zander level after Reclaim, while Zero follows Dungeon Guide with Displace to reach Lorraine level three.

Prismatic Edge and Imperious Galebind remove two Gleaming Cuts while Ghosts of Pendragon refill Zero’s hand. Jett uses Calming Breeze, then negates one Crux Sight; a second Sight returns Ascension. Further Edge triggers remove Windmill Engineer and Luxem Sight.

Jett retrieves Incapacitate at level two and finds Heavenly Guide to reach level three, but has little influence left. Zero has allies and weapons on board and finishes with Spirit Blade: Retribution, tying the final 2-2.

games.summary: Jett wins — Lightweaver's Assault and Gleaming Cut fuel the final push; Assassin's Ripper, Windmill Engineer and Aesan Protector close the match

beats.text: Jett’s opening Fairy Whispers misses on a wind card while keeping powerful draws on top. Turbo Charge rebuilds his influence, and Stifling Gyre names Ghosts of Pendragon. Benediction Angel and Aesan Protector pressure Zero, whose hand is crowded with advanced-element cards before he can reach level three.

Jett reaches Zander level two, activates Poisoned Dagger and attempts a prepared Slice and Dice. Zero answers with two Veiling Breezes through Nullifying Mirror, preventing the hit. Zero then finds Dungeon Guide, reaches Lorraine level three, and destroys Stifling Gyre with Verdigris Decree; Jett uses Heavenly Guide to reach his own level three.

Zero0000000000 rebuilds influence with Ghosts of Pendragon and plays Regal Inquisition. Jett responds with Lightweaver's Assault, revealing two Gleaming Cuts to draw four cards and dealing eight damage despite Clarent. Jett then swings with Assassin's Ripper for three, taking Zero0000000000 to 23 damage. Windmill Engineer and Aesan Protector provide the last five damage, making Jett the 2026 world champion.

games.summary: Matt wins — Ignis Deus blows out a Sudden Steel, then Volcanic Crescendo through the Lantern

beats.text: Matt starts with a draw-heavy hand: Creative Shock pitches a Liminal Guide, Cremation Ritual, Hasty Messenger and bobbles, and Backstep enables Torching Reach. He has the Fireball and melody in hand within two turns.

Nov finds Dungeon Guide and puts Palvor Sword on the board to banish Matt's graveyard face down, pairing it with Mantle of the Abyss and Rile the Abyss. Then Nullifying Lantern lands, so Matt has both a Sword and a Lantern to remove.

Nov goes for lethal at level one with Sudden Steel and Palvor Sword swings. Matt answers with Ignis Deus, which banishes the float, takes Tristan for four extra life and Agility 3, draws two from Liminal Guides, and makes the attack not lethal. Nov is hands down and has no interaction left.

Novephilion’s Sudden Steel consumes Palvor Sword during the failed lethal attempt, returning the banished graveyard cards. Matt finds Spurn to Ash for the remaining Nullifying Lantern, then materializes Discordia, Harp of Malice. With little life left, he plays Volcanic Crescendo without harmonize to avoid damaging himself, then finishes with an empowered Fireball for a 2-0 win.

matches.round: Round 12 (Day 2, Round 3) — Wind Razorgale Arisanna against Fire Oblation Ciel

sideboardNotes.text: The casters expect DuckHats to add Innervate Agility (spell shroud against Ciel’s spell trigger), Stifling Gyre against Dungeon Guide, Obscured Offering to protect the Orb of Sealing and Crystallized Destiny.

games.summary: DuckHats wins — Orb of Sealing and Veiling Breeze protect the setup for two Razorgale Callings

beats.text: Bandit, Gaze Leader fails to find another raccoon. Bocol123 uses Angelic Channeling to set up two Baleful Oblations, then omens Advent of the Stormcaller from hand. DuckHats returns Bandit with Aesan Protector and materializes Orb of Sealing to threaten the face-up omens.

Bocol123 adds a Golden Checkmate omen, and DuckHats uses Orb of Sealing to turn the omens face down. Later, Bocol123 establishes Manxome Armoire to exchange an omen with a card in hand. Both players preserve resources for the possible Oblation response chain.

DuckHats brings out Essence Crucible early (Bocol123 has no main-deck way to remove it) and then Arisanna. Aesan Protector hits for three each turn and two Distilled Waters put two counters on the Crucible, but DuckHats cannot find a Razorgale Calling with Cyclical Breeze and Fairy Whispers and has to hold up interaction.

Bocol123 holds two Baleful Oblations and Umbra Sight. Topsy Decree, imbued, gives him spell shroud for the turn, so Razorgale Calling can only hit DuckHats. Devouring Malice is answered by Skirting Step, and Chalice of Blood draws more cards.

Aesan Protector attacks and DuckHats plays a second Razorgale Calling, making another wind activation lethal. Bocol123 responds with Baleful Oblation; DuckHats activates Orb of Sealing, and Bocol123 plays a second Oblation. Veiling Breeze lets DuckHats survive the exchange and take game one.

games.summary: DuckHats wins — Essence Crucible reaches three counters, and three Veiling Breezes answer the Oblation attempt

beats.text: Bocol123 takes the first turn and passes, and DuckHats digs with Fairy Whispers but has no Razorgale. Another Bandit, Gaze Leader misses, and Bocol123 draws only clunky fire cards and a non-imbued Angel Attendant.

Windmill Engineer, Reclaim and Backup Charger build DuckHats’s hand. After Razorgale Calling and a brewed Speed Potion, he plays Stifling Gyre; the casters identify Dungeon Guide as its likely named card. Bocol123 removes Razorgale Calling with Expel the Departed, and DuckHats later recovers it with Cyclical Breeze.

Bocol123 loses Blanche to a level-up, then uses Cremation Ritual on Angel Attendant to draw three. A later Cremation sacrifices Liminal Guide, which Bandit banishes. After reaching level three, Bocol123 materializes his own Orb of Sealing to hide cheap omens before using Manxome Armoire to put Golden Checkmate into the omen zone.

DuckHats builds Essence Crucible to three counters. Bocol123 draws with Chalice of Blood, then uses Orb of Sealing, Manxome Armoire and Topsy Decree while attempting an Oblation finish. DuckHats responds with his own Orb and three Veiling Breezes, surviving the attempt and taking the match 2-0.

matches.round: Round 13 (Day 2, Round 4 — final Swiss round) — Fire Oblation Ciel against Fire Suzaku Guo Jia, a win-and-in for Top 8

sideboardNotes.text: The casters recommend Infernal Vessel against Abnegation, Crystallized Destiny against Oblation, and additional regalia removal for Mechsniper. Infernal Vessel is revealed in game two, but is not materialized during the reviewed sequence.

The casters discuss Blanche, Sheltering Saint and Nullifying Lantern for 1wisp, with the Lantern intended to stop Suzaku returning. Abnegation is seen in games two and three. Exact boarding counts are not confirmed.

games.summary: Wisp wins — a defensive Feu Awakening chain machine-guns Mechsniper out

beats.text: Wisp goes first and levels into CL with Library Witch as an interceptor. Cremation Ritual and Creative Shock dig for a 15-cost card, and a Dungeon Guide takes CL to level three through a quiz and Lost Providence.

Mechsniper plays Vermilion Decree for quest counters, Fiery Interference on the Dungeon Guide and Enfeebling Orb, reaches six quest counters, and flips Suzaku, the Vermilion Phoenix. Mechsniper hurts himself with Fabled Ruby Fatestone, which puts Wisp's Oblation in range at four damage.

Mechsniper uses Enfeebling Orb and Shatter the Brittle to remove Tariff Ring, then pushes damage with Suzaku and Impact Hammer. Peppered Chef sacrifices Suzaku so it can return ready, with Blazing Throw available to threaten lethal.

Wisp has only about four total influence, so he discards his whole hand to Feu Awakening, which makes two omens that kill the Peppered Chef. Manxome Armoire then swaps Feu Awakening back so each omen shoots again. The chain deals the last damage and ends the game.

games.summary: Mechsniper wins — Avatar of Suzaku start, Wisp's Feu Awakening line is one damage short

beats.text: Mechsniper plays Avatar of Suzaku on turn one, Fabled Ruby Fatestone and Searing Truth for two quest counters, and reaches five quest counters while Wisp tries to level. Wisp uses Angelic Channeling, banishing two Golden Checkmates, and holds two Dungeon Guides.

Impact Hammer, Spark Alight and Suzaku threaten a fast kill. 1wisp uses Resolute Stand, levels to Ciel, Omenbringer, and follows with Dungeon Guide. He loses Abnegation while leveling; Infernal Vessel has been revealed but is not yet on the field. Mechsniper materializes Grand Crusader’s Ring and continues adding damage and quest counters.

1wisp materializes Manxome Armoire after using a second Resolute Stand. The casters calculate a double-Feu line but find it short. Mechsniper targets Armoire with Shatter the Brittle; 1wisp responds by retrieving Resolute Stand, leaving Feu Awakening in the omen zone.

After another Resolute Stand, 1wisp uses Chalice of Blood to rebuild from no cards. Mechsniper plays Restorative Flame before the next Feu Awakening sequence. 1wisp uses Ciel’s Lineage Release for Feu and adds end-phase omen damage, but finishes one damage short. Mechsniper closes the game to tie the match.

games.summary: Mechsniper wins — Fiery Interference stops an Abnegation, then Avatar of Suzaku flips the Phoenix

beats.text: Wisp goes first with Cremation Ritual, Creative Shock and Resolute Stand in a keepable hand. A Liminal Guide level up and Cremation Ritual for value show Wisp is playing a low-influence game, with Wisp one level up while Mechsniper plays Three of Hearts and Fabled Ruby Fatestone.

Wisp levels to CL level three with Dungeon Guide and omens Advent of the Stormcaller, putting Baleful Oblation in the 15-damage range. Wisp holds Resolute Stand and Abnegation. Mechsniper holds only reactive cards, two Vermilion Decrees and Ember Crypt Burn.
Mechsniper attacks with his ally board and Impact Hammer, bringing 1wisp to 20 damage while the Hammer puts Mechsniper at 11. 1wisp holds Resolute Stand instead of using it during the attacks.

Blazing Throw goes to Wisp's face, Wisp responds with Abnegation and Mechsniper answers with Fiery Interference, taking Wisp to 24 and then 28. The last two cards activate Avatar of Suzaku for the final quest counters, Suzaku flips and ends the game. Mechsniper wins 2-1 and locks Top 8.

games.summary: Isaac wins — Flame Sweep clears the allies and Devastating Blow punishes the missing Shadowdancer defense

beats.text: Tress develops Censer of Restful Peace, shutting off Isaac’s floating memory, and delays his own Tristan level-up while building resources. Isaac pressures with Fluffy Shopkeep, Three of Hearts and Inert Sword, then leaves Stalwart Shieldmate available to defend.

Tress’s Tariff Ring leaves Isaac one card short of Flame Sweep on the Lorraine level-two turn. The casters discuss a possible Slice and Dice line into Isaac’s held Resolute Stand, but Tress instead levels through Dungeon Guide to Shadowreaver and attacks with allies.

games.summary: TeamTrueIsaac wins — Devastating Blow with Sword of Seeking's true sight is lethal because Spirit of Wind has too little life

Isaac’s Flame Sweep is blunted when Tress returns Sadi, Reclaims Aesan Protector and plays Veiling Breeze. Tress loses Slice and Dice while leveling to Tristan. Isaac’s later Dungeon Guide resolves after Tress’s Surveil the Winds fails to find a stopping response.

games.summary: TeppeSlorn wins — Spirelle slows Rai and Beguiling Coup turns into Heavy Swing

beats.text: TeppeSlorn again reaches Ciel level three and develops Spirelle. Hyouka uses Disorienting Winds to replay Dungeon Guide, but loses Mnemonic Charm and Careful Study on the next level-up. Spirelle negates Scry the Skies, forcing Hyouka to rebuild his setup.

Hyouka survives with Three Visits and Resolute Stand; a later omen trigger removes Dungeon Guide instead of hitting Rai.

games.summary: Perfy wins — early Merlin pressure and Ghosts of Pendragon leave Guruthos unable to survive the Fireballs

games.summary: Xenadrael wins — defensive wind activations keep Razorgale damage accumulating through a long first game

beats.text: Xenadrael opens with Windmill Engineer and Eternal Magistrate while searching for Razorgale Calling. Bratus develops Baby Green Slime and allies, choosing normal level-ups around Magistrate’s timing restriction. Xenadrael uses Tempest Downfall against Shimmercloak Assassin and Zephyr to interrupt Displace on Brisk Windtrotter.

Xenadrael later finds his own Innervate Agility while under heavy attack pressure.

Xenadrael uses Ventus to suppress Seiryuu, follows with Dream Fairy and keeps Veiling Breeze available. Bratus’s Beastbond Boots threaten to prevent Razorgale damage, creating a standoff over Tempest Downfall. Xenadrael levels back up for a life buffer and uses Stifling Trap to remove Shimmercloak Assassin. With Bratus reduced to one remaining damage, another wind activation closes game one.

games.summary: Xenadrael wins — Ardent Cloudstriker pressure followed by Tempest Downfall finishes the match

beats.text: Bratus starts with Beseeched Fatestone before Eternal Magistrate can interfere. Xenadrael develops Ardent Cloudstriker and reaches Kongming, preparing to attack for six with Shifting Currents pointing west. The casters prefer using Bagua to draw cards over adding buff counters to Cloudstriker.

Bratus transforms Beseeched Fatestone into a blocking threat, but Xenadrael Zephyrs it before pushing damage with Cloudstriker and Magistrate. Bratus then uses Displace on Eternal Magistrate, removing its imbued status and opening a later level-up window.
Xenadrael follows with Tempest Downfall, Cyclical Breeze and another Tempest Downfall to finish the match. He wins 2-0 and takes the Ascent Niagara Falls title.

Noel concedes after Lifdrasyl establishes level 3 with a large influence advantage. The game ends before a damaging finishing sequence is played.

games.summary: Noel wins — growing allies overwhelm repeated Luxem Sight healing

beats.text: Noel uses Searing Rebuke with Impact Hammer’s self-damage, then attacks with Vanitas. Lifdrasyl allows the Rebuke to resolve, and the attack pushes Zander to 22 damage before the next healing cycle.

Brisk Windtrotter buffs and Beastsoul Visage make Noel’s allies difficult to clear. Lifdrasyl uses Lightweaver’s Assault defensively to heal and remove Dilu, but Red Hare, Lava Soul Tiger and Vanitas keep the pressure high.

JacePatrick uses Feu Awakening to remove Frostsworn Paladin and strengthen Grande Sonnerie’s attack. Royan survives and uses Revitalizing Cleanse. On the next turn, Enfeebling Orb restricts JacePatrick’s hand, Fracturize removes Folded Shadows, and Genbu with Resonating Fugue closes the match 2-0.

matches.sourceNote: The Gauntlet 2026 broadcast transcript, Round 3. Recap claims checked against gameplay windows. Folded Shadows protects JacePatrick’s Ciel; Royan removes it with Fracturize before the final Genbu/Fugue line.

matches.round: Round 4: Fire Oblation Ciel against Water Exia Jin mill

sideboardNotes.text: The casters discuss Abnegation and Blanche against Jin’s damage options, and Annul Spell against Dynastic Whirlpool and Regal Inquisition. These are recommendations rather than confirmed swaps.

Dal157 switches to Spirit of Serene Water for game two. The casters also discuss Chime of Endless Dreams, Tabula of Salvage and Delusional Vapors; those comments do not confirm that each card was brought in.

games.summary: Dal157 wins — TheRainGoddess never finds Baleful Oblation and the Dynastic Whirlpool mills the deck out

beats.text: TheRainGoddess keeps the opening hand but has to be careful: against mill, each extra card drawn pulls the deck closer to empty. She removes a lantern and an Orb of Sealing from the material deck to draw an additional card.

TheRainGoddess uses Angelic Channeling to set up advanced-element cards. Dal157 uses Fracturize on his own Power Cell for a reservable fractal, but TheRainGoddess’s Topsy Decree denies the floating memory. Dal157 spends early turns drawing and setting up Jin while Fluffy Shopkeep attacks.

Dal157 survives heavy damage through Pearled Prayer, Mend Flesh and Regenerate, then mills with Dynastic Whirlpool. TheRainGoddess draws deeper through Devouring Malice and Umbra Sight but cannot find Baleful Oblation. Another 15-card mill and Bauble of Abundance leave no escape, and TheRainGoddess concedes.

games.summary: TheRainGoddess wins — a fast draw engine builds repeated Oblation pressure through Jin’s recovery

beats.text: TheRainGoddess hits five plus three with Rictus Tiding, then uses Backup Charger and Turbo Charge to build influence. Creative Shock discards Liminal Guide for the level-up, followed by Library Witch and Cremation Ritual. Topsy Decree again interferes with Dal157’s Angelic Channeling setup.

Oblation and Devastating Blow force Dal157 into recovery. He uses Chalice of Blood, Seething Intercession, Transfusive Aura and Pearled Prayer, while TheRainGoddess keeps Lost Providence available to support another finishing sequence.
Dal157 releases Spirit of Serene Water and benefits from Transfusive Aura, but another Baleful Oblation followed by Feu Awakening supplies enough damage to end game two. The match is tied 1-1.

games.summary: Draw — Jin’s recovery leaves TheRainGoddess one damage short as time expires

beats.text: Dal157 goes first and keeps Spirit of Serene Water. TheRainGoddess holds Liminal Guide, Angelic Channeling and Angel Attendant, but initially lacks Cremation Ritual. Both players must develop quickly with only a few minutes remaining.

TheRainGoddess uses Topsy Decree against Dal157’s Angelic Channeling setup. Dal157 later Fracturizes his own Power Cell to help level. TheRainGoddess draws with Creative Shock and Cremation Ritual, finding multiple Oblations, while Dal157 uses two Dungeon Guides to reach Jin, Undying Resolve.

Dal157 materializes Berserker Plate and uses Pearled Prayers to recover during the extra turns. He releases Spirit of Serene Water between Oblations. TheRainGoddess adds Feu Awakening and Manxome Armoire damage, but Lost Providence fails to draw the additional Feu needed. The final line is one damage short, and time ends the match 1-1.

matches.sourceNote: The Gauntlet 2026 broadcast transcript, Round 4. Recap claims checked against opening and finishing windows. The 45-damage recovery and Whirlpool sequence belong to game one, not game three. The 1-1 draw awards neither player a Gauntlet win.

matches.round: Round 5: Fire Oblation Ciel against Fire Suzaku Guo Jia

sideboardNotes.text: The casters recommend Annul Spell and consider another Restorative Flame for Jayare. Annul is seen in his game-two hand.
The casters discuss Annul Spell, Blanche and Flamewreath Call for Guruthos. Blanche is discarded in game two; Flamewreath Call appears in game three but is also discarded rather than played.

games.summary: Guruthos wins — survives Jayare’s double-Destiny turn, then finishes with Grande Sonnerie and omen damage

beats.text: Guruthos opens Dungeon Guide without using its level-up effect, then develops Ciel through Angelic Channeling and another Guide. Jayare opens Liminal Guide, sacrifices it with Undeniable Truth before leveling, and develops Avatar of Suzaku and quest counters.

Guruthos removes Jayare’s Orb of Sealing with Nocturne’s Oblivion, then materializes Manxome Armoire. During Jayare’s attack turn, Guruthos casts Baleful Oblation. Armoire breaks the first Crystallized Destiny, but Jayare has a second Destiny to prevent the Oblation damage to his champion. Suzaku returns and attacks, leaving Guruthos at 25 damage.

Guruthos materializes Grande Sonnerie, banishing Turbo Charge, and draws Feu Awakening. Ciel attacks for five; the end-phase omen adds the final two damage. Jayare has no fire cards left in the graveyard to support Restorative Flame, and Guruthos takes game one.

games.summary: Jayare wins — Fiery Interference denies recovery, and Orb of Sealing blanks the defensive Oblation

beats.text: Jayare goes first with Creative Shock and Liminal Guide, then clears Guruthos’s Fluffy Shopkeep with Demolition. Avatar of Suzaku and Vengeful Paramour build an ally-heavy board. Guruthos develops Angel Attendant and keeps Resolute Stand, discarding Blanche while leveling.

Guruthos uses Resolute Stand for its alternate cost, then materializes Chalice of Blood. Jayare cannot imbue Vermilion Decree with only two fire cards in hand, but uses Fiery Interference to add a quest counter and prevent recovery. Chalice draws Guruthos Abnegation, which cannot heal that turn.

Jayare uses Peppered Chef with Suzaku and activates Suzaku’s Command before the Chef’s attack. Guruthos attempts Baleful Oblation to clear the board, but Jayare’s Orb of Sealing turns the omen face down. The zero-damage Oblation cannot stop the lethal attack.

games.summary: Guruthos wins — Manxome Armoire restores the 15-cost omen for a decisive main-phase Oblation

beats.text: Guruthos goes first while Jayare develops two Vengeful Paramours. Guruthos holds Flamewreath Call but does not use it. Jayare’s Embercrypt Burn removes Angelic Channeling from the graveyard, forcing Guruthos to pay two cards to level; Ciel’s on-enter then discards Flamewreath Call.

Guruthos uses Dungeon Guide to reach Ciel’s third level with low influence. Jayare materializes Orb of Sealing. Guruthos chooses Manxome Armoire instead of Chalice of Blood, preparing an immediate Oblation attempt.

Guruthos plays Baleful Oblation in his main phase. Jayare activates Orb of Sealing, but Manxome Armoire returns Golden Checkmate to hand and places it back as a face-up omen. Jayare lacks the needed defense, and Guruthos wins 2-1.

matches.sourceNote: The Gauntlet 2026 broadcast transcript, Round 5; gameplay reviewed from 384:00–430:59. Game-two Fiery Interference and Abnegation are not part of the game-three finish. Jayare controls the defensive Orb of Sealing in games two and three.

matches.round: Round 6: Wind Crux Lorraine against Fire Oblation Ciel

sideboardNotes.text: The casters discuss Orb of Sealing and Chamberlain Toad for GlenyBoi. Both are seen in game two, with the Toad supplying a water card for Prismatic Edge.

games.summary: GlenyBoi wins — Ascension rips Limelight's memory apart and Prismatic Edge pushes the last damage

beats.text: GlenyBoi levels through two Dungeon Guides after Limelight removes Sword of Seeking with Reduce to Ash. Drawn Blade returns, letting Lorraine attack Library Witch for a draw. Two Ghosts of Pendragon then rebuild GlenyBoi’s hand.

After Limelight clears the board with Baleful Oblation, GlenyBoi uses Spirit Blade: Ascension and Crux Sight to repeatedly return Prismatic Edge. Memory banishes remove Oblation and other threats; Aella adds another suppression cycle. Fairy Whispers and Scout the Land find further Ascensions.

Limelight survives with Resolute Stand and later uses Devouring Malice to deal three and recover three. Another Ascension banishes his newly drawn Oblation. GlenyBoi replaces Aella under the unique rule and finishes with ally damage and Lorraine’s Prismatic Edge attack.

games.summary: GlenyBoi wins — Galebind on Manxome Armoire blunts Oblation, then Ascension finishes through Feu

beats.text: GlenyBoi builds resources with Fluffy Shopkeep, Reclaim and Aesan Protector before leveling Lorraine. In response to Limelight’s Dungeon Guide, Ascension brings back Prismatic Edge; Annul Spell stops Crux Sight, but Edge still banishes Spirelle from memory. A later Ascension banishes Undeniable Truth.

Limelight attempts Baleful Oblation with Manxome Armoire available. GlenyBoi uses Imperious Galebind on the Armoire rather than only his own value pieces, keeping the Oblation at three damage and preserving Aella. Limelight sacrifices Dungeon Guide to draw Carter, then uses Carter and an omen trigger to remove Ghosts of Pendragon.

With Limelight low on cards, GlenyBoi presses with his board and Prismatic Edge. Limelight uses Feu Awakening to try to remove Aella, but GlenyBoi responds with Crux Sight to retrieve Spirit Blade: Ascension. The Ascension finishes the match 2-0.

matches.sourceNote: The Gauntlet 2026 broadcast transcript, Round 6. Recap claims checked against 458:00–496:59. Limelight’s registered sideboard confirms Spirelle, Schwartz Queen. Game-two Galebind targets Manxome Armoire to limit Oblation; the earlier Crux Sight is negated and banished.

games.summary: DuckHats wins — Cleansing Reunion disrupts Reflected Blight and ProAnnn concedes

Song of Frost could be the one card to bring in against Devastating Blow variants, but he feels strong about his Oblation matchup.

games.summary: Raylam wins — ally pressure and Feu Awakening overwhelm Caban’s defense

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban Fracturizes his Powercell, then uses its floating-memory card for Frostsworn Paladin. Raylam sacrifices the threatened Hasty Messenger to Undeniable Truth. Three of Hearts and another Messenger later clear the Paladin.

Raylam reaches Ciel, Omenbringer and draws from Liminal Guide, then uses Dungeon Guide to reach Mirage’s Grave. Caban builds fractals but remains at level zero after materializing Enfeebling Orb; the casters calculate that his available damage and influence fall short.

Raylam attacks with his allies. Caban uses Enfeebling Orb and targets Hasty Messenger with Shimmering Refraction, but Raylam shows Feu Awakening and Caban concedes. The casters discuss leveling to Diao Chan as a possible alternative in hindsight, not an established misplay.

games.summary: TeamTrueCaban wins — Raylam survives Burst Asunder, but later falls to Refracting Missile

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban opens with an imbued Fractal of Rain and a hand with Refracting Missile, Zhang Jiao and a Glimmering Refusal, everything a Fractals player wants except more fractals. He takes far less pressure than in game one.

Caban develops his fractals and deals damage with Refracting Missile. Raylam reaches Ciel, Omenbringer but cannot find Dungeon Guide. Caban holds Glimmering Refusal for Raylam’s defensive Topsy Decree.

Caban answers Topsy Decree with two Glimmering Refusals. Raylam uses Feu Awakening at level two, discarding his hand and memory so Topsy resolves and grants spellshroud against Burst Asunder. Caban retains his fractals. On a later turn, Shimmering Refraction adds damage; Enfeebling Orb empties Raylam’s hand before Refracting Missile finishes the game.

games.summary: Raylam wins — a third Baleful Oblation breaks through after two are negated

beats.text: Raylam plays a wide aggressive ally strategy, which the casters say is not what Oblation CL usually does but works to pressure Fractals. Fluffy Shopkeep banishes a key card, and Raylam discards a Floating Memory he does not need.

Caban spends Refracting Missile to remove Hasty Messenger. Fractal of Intrusion later discards Raylam’s Incapacitate from memory. Caban then uses Glimmering Refusal on Fluffy Shopkeep to deny Raylam its draw.

Caban negates Raylam’s first two Baleful Oblations. On the following turn, Raylam materializes Manxome Armoire and uses Lost Providence before recollection. A third Oblation resolves after Acquiescing Rejection; the ensuing omen damage and Armoire activation finish the game.

matches.sourceNote: Worlds 2026 Swiss Stage VOD, Round 2. Captions at 138:31–183:14 establish the game order and Raylam’s 2–1 win; targeted interview passages at 191:38–193:55 were also checked. matches.result: Draw 1-1 (game 3 ran out of time; double loss)

The casters discuss Annul Spell, Calming Breeze and more attack cards as Lifdrasyl’s options. Annul Spell is visible in game two; exact swaps are not shown.

games.summary: Lifdrasyl wins — repeated Prismatic Edge triggers exhaust Asuna’s hand

beats.text: Asuna establishes two imbued Eternal Magistrates. Lifdrasyl suppresses one with Verdigris Decree, removing its imbue, then attacks the other after leveling to Lorraine, Blademaster. Asuna reclaims it, opening the way for Lifdrasyl to reach level three.

Asuna eventually finds Razorgale Calling with Fairy Whispers and builds toward multiple Razorgales. Lifdrasyl’s Aella repeatedly suppresses Essence Crucible, removing its accumulated counters, while Asuna uses Veiling Breeze to keep combat damage out.

Imperious Galebind reuses Aella, Ghosts of Pendragon and Prismatic Edge, helping Lifdrasyl find his fire card and cut Asuna’s influence. On Asuna’s next turn, Enfeebling Orb forces more cards down. Displace reuses Aella for another Prismatic Edge trigger showing all three elements; Asuna concedes.

games.summary: Asuna wins — three Razorgale triggers with Essence Crucible end the game faster than a Razorgale hit the field in game one

beats.text: Lifdrasyl builds influence with Fluffy Shopkeep and Escape the Wreckage. Asuna levels early, establishes Razorgale Calling and brings out Essence Crucible. The casters later question whether Lifdrasyl lacks Dungeon Guide or is playing around Stifling Trap.

Asuna finds all three Razorgales, while the casters identify a single Verdigris Decree as Lifdrasyl’s answer. Speed Potion helps Asuna recover cards, and Three Visits plus a reclaim set up the remaining damage.

Asuna plays the second and third Razorgales, adding their damage triggers. Essence Crucible boosts the closing damage; the casters explain that Annul Spell cannot stop the Razorgale triggers even if it negates the spell. Asuna ties the match.

games.summary: No winner — time runs out with both players in a tense position, and the round ends as a double loss

beats.text: Lifdrasyl has Verdigris Decree in his opening hand and develops Windmill Engineer. Asuna’s imbued Eternal Magistrate attacks the Engineer, which Lifdrasyl reclaims. Lifdrasyl then levels to Lorraine, Wandering Warrior and brings out Sword of Seeking.

Lifdrasyl plays Dream Fairy targeting Eternal Magistrate. Asuna saves it with Escape the Wreckage and then plays Stifling Gyre instead of replaying Magistrate. The later commentary confirms Gyre names Ghosts of Pendragon. Asuna also uses Incapacitate to stop Ascension after its Sword cost is paid.

In overtime, both players keep Veiling Breeze available. Lifdrasyl materializes Sword of Seeking and shows Spirit Blade: Retribution, but lacks enough influence to activate it. Neither player wins the game; the broadcast confirms a 1–1 draw, worth no match points in this Worlds format.

games.summary: Superior wins — Enfeebling Orb clears the way for Genbu and Resonating Fugue, backed by Frostbind

beats.text: TheRainGoddess uses Censer of Restful Peace to shut off Superior’s graveyard abilities, with Nullifying Lantern also available in the material deck. The casters note Superior has only two Unbroken Mustangs and may need Fracturize to answer the Censer.

beats.text: Superior shows Beastbond Boots and mills Expel the Departed. He holds Fracturize and removes TheRainGoddess’s Censer of Restful Peace. Later, Throne-Keeper Bullfrog enters with two buff counters alongside Tidestone Bovine and the growing ally board.

players.deck: Wind Crux Lorraine, Spirit Ruler (Ghosts of Pendragon, Spirit Blade: Ascension, Prismatic Edge, Aella; Eternal Magistrate and Crystallized Destiny in the sideboard)

sideboardNotes.text: Jett brings in the Eternal Magistrate. The casters call it a thorn in Guruthos's side for games two and three, because it also stops Lost Providence from being activated in the main phase and gives Lorraine time to reach level three.

Before game three, the casters correct their initial Flamewreath Call boarding claim after noticing Guruthos is holding his sideboard. They report Flamewreath Call, Nocturne’s Oblivion, and Heavenly Guide being left out or removed. They discuss Call as a possible answer to Eternal Magistrate; no copy counts are established.

games.summary: Guruthos wins — an initial Oblation punishes Orb of Sealing, then two more beat Veiling Breeze

beats.text: Guruthos uses Creative Shock and Angelic Channeling to prepare fifteen-cost cards and Baleful Oblations. Jett establishes Orb of Sealing, then uses Dungeon Guide and Displace to reach Lorraine, Spirit Ruler before Guruthos reaches level three.

Guruthos orders his level-up triggers so Liminal Guide draws Baleful Oblation, leaving another Oblation and a fifteen-cost card near the top. Lost Providence enters play, while Jett’s Orb of Sealing threatens the fifteen-cost omen.

Guruthos plays the first Baleful Oblation in response to Jett’s Orb of Sealing. On Jett’s next turn, Ghosts of Pendragon rebuild the ally board and draw cards; one returns Enfeebling Orb to the material deck, leaving it unavailable to disrupt Guruthos’s next turn.

Guruthos materializes Manxome Armoire, draws Advent of the Stormcaller with Umbra Sight, and adds it as an omen at end of turn. He plays Baleful Oblation. Jett digs with Crux Sight and Fairy Whispers, then attempts Veiling Breeze. Guruthos responds with another Oblation and uses Armoire to restore a fifteen-cost omen, winning before Breeze resolves.

games.summary: Jett wins — Eternal Magistrate delays Guruthos, and Imperious Galebind stops the Grande Sonnerie finish

beats.text: Jett uses Purifying Thurible to deny Guruthos’s floating memory, then Dungeon Guide and Displace to reach Lorraine, Spirit Ruler. Eternal Magistrate shuts off Guruthos’s Guide plays and Lost Providence activation outside materialization. Jett then materializes Orb of Sealing.

Jett plays Aella during recollection and attacks with his allies. Guruthos uses Chalice of Blood, Umbra Sight, and Abnegation to stay alive. Jett responds to Abnegation with two Spirit Blade: Ascensions: Prismatic Edge draws cards and removes two from Guruthos’s memory, but deals no fire damage. Abnegation then recovers ten.

Resolute Stand buys Guruthos another turn. He retains Baleful Oblation and materializes Grande Sonnerie, then finds another fifteen-cost card. Jett’s Imperious Galebind denies the weapon damage needed to finish. Guruthos concedes without executing the proposed Oblation–Feu Awakening line.

games.summary: Jett wins — Aella and Prismatic Edge deny Ciel level three, then Lorraine lands the final weapon attack

beats.text: Guruthos goes first and uses Creative Shock to discard Golden Checkmate before leveling, choosing speed over a Backup Charger turn. Gentle Respite gives him another draw and floating memory.

Jett plays Eternal Magistrate to block Guruthos’s Guide acceleration, then uses Dungeon Guide and Displace to reach Lorraine, Spirit Ruler himself. Ghosts of Pendragon builds his board. Spirit Blade: Ascension brings in Prismatic Edge, which reveals wind, water, and Guruthos’s fire card for the full effect, including three damage.

Guruthos has Baleful Oblation and Feu Awakening, and uses Resolute Stand’s alternate cost to preserve cards for leveling. Jett’s Aella suppresses Prismatic Edge; its end-step return removes memory and denies Ciel level three. Guruthos materializes Chalice of Blood instead. On Jett’s next turn, ally attacks trigger the Chalice draw, but Guruthos finds Gentle Respite rather than another Resolute Stand. Lorraine’s Prismatic Edge attack finishes the game.

matches.sourceNote: Worlds 2026 Swiss Stage VOD, Round 5; Jett wins 2–1 per Omnidex. Game-one finish checked at 406:02–417:43; games two and three checked at 419:04–456:34. Game two ends in concession after Imperious Galebind stops the proposed weapon finish. In game three Guruthos has Oblation, but Jett prevents Ciel level three before the final weapon attack. Boarding commentary includes an explicit correction about Flamewreath Call. Swiss attachments use Silvie.gg’s explicitly labeled Swiss lists. The game-one opening was also reviewed at 395:19–406:02; the casters speculate about trigger handling while a judge is present, but do not establish a missed-trigger penalty.

matches.round: Round 6: Water Fractals Diao Chan against Wind Razorgale Arisanna
matches.result: Asuna wins 2-1, ending Noel's undefeated run

sideboardNotes.text: The casters discuss Mystic Purifier, Scatter Essence, Stifling Gyre, Blessed Clergy and additional Calming Breeze as Asuna’s options. They do not confirm the cards exchanged.
The casters discuss Nullifying Mirror and Jianyu, Fate's Premonition as Noel’s options. Nullifying Mirror is subsequently shown in game two; exact swaps are not reported.

games.summary: Noel wins — Burst Asunder ends the game while Asuna is still on Gwendalin

beats.text: Noel reserves Fractal of Intrusion to cast Refracting Missile before Intrusion’s on-enter resolves, then uses the floating memory to discard Asuna’s Speed Potion. Asuna has already found an opening Razorgale Calling with Scout the Land.

Asuna materializes Viridian Protective Trinket and later plays Eternal Magistrate, imbuing it with two Three Visits. Noel builds fractals, deals four with Refracting Missile and materializes Nullifying Lantern.

Noel sends Burst Asunder while Asuna remains on Gwendolyn, Spirit of Wind. Asuna has no answer and loses game one. The two Three Visits are in memory; the casters’ discussion of whether keeping one would have saved him is inconclusive.

games.summary: Asuna wins — three Razorgales and Essence Crucible force Noel’s concession

beats.text: Asuna opens with Fluffy Shopkeep. Noel’s Acquiescing Rejection stops Reclaim when Asuna declines the draw. Noel later changes Fractal of Intrusion’s discard choice from Razorgale Calling to Stifling Trap; Asuna levels to Arisanna and establishes three Razorgales.
Noel materializes Nullifying Mirror and develops Fractal of Snow. Asuna brings out Essence Crucible, keeps Distilled Water through the level cost and finds Speed Potion for the closing turn.

Noel contests Speed Potion with Acquiescing Rejection and Glimmering Refusal. The casters explain that brewing still gives Essence Crucible its counter despite the negation. Noel concedes with further Razorgale damage available.

games.summary: Asuna wins — Obscured Offering protects Crucible, then three wind spells finish

beats.text: Noel opens with two Fractals of Snow and keeps Fracturize for Essence Crucible instead of using it to build another fractal. Asuna uses Reclaim while Noel is committed to Backup Charger, then levels to Arisanna and plays the discounted Razorgale Calling.

Asuna sets up Viridian Protective Trinket, Tend the Land and two Speed Potions. Noel responds to the second brew with Fracturize targeting Essence Crucible. Obscured Offering gives Crucible spellshroud, preserving its counters; the proposed defensive Zephyr is not the play used.
The Speed Potions recover cards through agility. In the end phase, Asuna plays Veiling Breeze, Calming Breeze and Three Visits for three Razorgale damage each, winning the match 2–1.

sideboardNotes.text: The casters propose Restorative Flame and Annul Spell as Jayare’s options against Baleful Oblation. They discuss Feu Awakening as counterplay to a negate; the recording does not establish the exact boarding changes.

games.summary: Raylam wins — Manxome Armoire restores a fifteen-cost omen for Baleful Oblation

beats.text: Jayare’s Three of Hearts attacks Raylam’s Hasty Messenger. Raylam plays Escape the Wreckage to save it, then replays Hasty and discards Ionized Asceticism to set up a fifteen-cost omen.

Jayare develops Fabled Ruby Fatestone, Searing Truth and Avatar of Suzaku. Raylam levels to Ciel, Omenbringer, discards Liminal Guide and uses Dungeon Guide to reach Mirage’s Grave; omen damage removes Avatar of Suzaku.

Jayare’s Orb of Sealing turns the omens face down. Raylam uses Manxome Armoire to restore the fifteen-cost omen and sends Baleful Oblation. Jayare digs with Creative Shock and Undeniable Truth but finds no saving Crystallized Destiny; Raylam wins game one.

games.summary: Jayare wins — Heated Vengeance, Impact Hammer and Blazing Throw end game two

beats.text: Jayare opens with Three of Hearts, and Raylam has the Hasty Messenger and Escape the Wreckage start again. Fiery Interference comes down before the Ruby Fate Stone, so Jayare does not get the quest counter. Raylam discards a Liminal Guide, and the casters say a double Three of Hearts would have turned it for him.
The casters call out the cards in Jayare's grip: Impact Hammer, Heated Vengeance and Blazing Throw, with all the pieces for a lethal turn two into four.

Jayare plays Heated Vengeance into a big swing at Raylam's face, hits with the Impact Hammer, and throws it with Blazing Throw. Raylam has no answer. The casters call it an insane turn-two Turbo line and say the two games took only 15 minutes. Raylam goes on to win game three, which the VOD does not show.

sideboardNotes.text: The casters discuss Annul Spell, Calming Breeze, Chamberlain Toad and Psychopomp’s Scale as GlenyBoi’s options. Annul Spell is subsequently played in game two; exact swaps are not shown.

DuckHats plays imbued Eternal Magistrate in game two. It restricts GlenyBoi’s material deck outside GlenyBoi’s materialize phase, leaving DuckHats free to use his own Dungeon Guides. The broadcast also discusses Annul Spell and Calming Breeze as options.

games.summary: GlenyBoi wins — repeated Prismatic Edge triggers and Ghosts draws force a concession

beats.text: Both players build influence with Fluffy Shopkeep and Backup Charger. DuckHats reaches Lorraine, Blademaster with Dungeon Guide. When GlenyBoi later uses Displace to level, DuckHats responds with his own Displace before the opposing Prismatic Edge engine can strip his memory.
GlenyBoi develops Ghosts of Pendragon and Spirit Blade: Ascension, keeping DuckHats low on influence through Prismatic Edge. A fire card in memory enables damage as well as the wind effect.

Imperious Galebind suppresses Prismatic Edge and Ghosts of Pendragon. The returning Ghosts put Sword of Seeking back and draw two. DuckHats draws Retribution without enough influence to use it and concedes.

games.summary: GlenyBoi wins — Annul Spell opens the level-up, then Aella and Ascension take over

beats.text: DuckHats reveals Eternal Magistrate while imbuing an Engineer, then plays Magistrate to constrain GlenyBoi. DuckHats breaks a hard-materialized Drawn Blade in combat and reaches level three ahead of GlenyBoi.

GlenyBoi’s Rally the Peasants misses. He later uses Annul Spell against DuckHats’s Imperious Galebind, gets the Lorraine draw and finds Dungeon Guide. That lets him reach Spirit Ruler, then play Ghosts of Pendragon and find Ascension.

GlenyBoi draws more Ghosts, Aella and Ascension. Aella suppresses Prismatic Edge, and Crux Sight returns Ascension for another Edge trigger. DuckHats loses more memory cards and concedes without finding the Crux cards to recover.

matches.round: Round 8: Water Fractals Diao Chan against Wind Crux Lorraine

sideboardNotes.text: TeamTrueCaban brings out Nullifying Mirror in game two. The casters discuss its value against Veiling Breeze and wind imbue effects. Quicksilver Grail is a comparison; his registered divine relic is The Looking Glass.
Sano has Annul Spell in game two and plays it during the final exchange. The casters discuss Calming Breeze and Crystallized Destiny as possible additions; exact swaps are not shown.

games.summary: TeamTrueCaban wins — he goes first with five fractals and Zhang Jiao, and Sano concedes

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban goes first with an imbued Fractal of Rain and builds toward Zhang Jiao, Way of Peace. He bottoms an extra Acquiescing Rejection and Burst Asunder while setting up the draw.

The casters note that Sano's list has no Clarent, so he has less defense against Burst Asunder. Sano has no Stifling Trap to stop the Zhang Jiao draws. TeamTrueCaban has eight cards in hand and four fractals, effectively 12 influence, with Glimmering Refusals backing up the kill turn.

Sano plays Purifying Thurible and stays on his spirit with five fractals staring him down. The casters call it a default win for TeamTrueCaban, who only had to play the cards, and Sano concedes early to keep time for game two. The casters say TM32 are happy to concede early with Wind Krux to avoid a double loss.

games.summary: TeamTrueCaban wins — Nullifying Mirror limits Sano’s answers to the final Burst Asunder

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban uses Acquiescing Rejection on Fluffy Shopkeep. Sano allows the two-card draw, so Shopkeep resolves. TeamTrueCaban later uses Fractal of Intrusion to discard Ghosts of Pendragon, then kills Shopkeep with Refracting Missile.

Nullifying Mirror turns Sano’s memory cards norm, limiting Windmill Engineer’s imbue and Veiling Breeze. Sano uses Verdigris Decree on a fractal, but TeamTrueCaban’s Shimmering Refraction removes an Engineer before it can help Lorraine finish Frostsworn Paladin. The Paladin keeps attacking.

Three Shimmering Refractions and attacks from Frostsworn Paladin and Zhang Jiao set up Burst Asunder. TeamTrueCaban pays for Sano’s Annul Spell. Sano has only one Veiling Breeze against the held Nullifying Mirror and concedes the match.

matches.round: Round 1 (Day 1) — 2025 World Champion in a round-one pairing

players.name: Dit
players.deck: Water Genbu Guo Jia (Fractal of Polar Depths mill-out)

players.name: boeboe
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (Fatestone / Angelic Channeling main deck)

matches.result: Dit wins 2-1 (game 3 awarded after a game loss to boeboe)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters recommend Nullifying Lantern, Psychopomp's Gale and Dream Fairy for boeboe. They also consider Expel the Departed because Dit exposed Polar Depths before gaining its class bonus. Lantern is shown and Gale is identified in hand in game two; exact swap counts are unconfirmed.
The casters predict Dit brings in the third Unbroken Mustang, Song of Frost and the last Engulf, to answer the Lantern and the dragon combo. These are caster predictions, not a confirmed list.

games.summary: Dit wins by Polar Depths mill-out

beats.text: Dit opens Fractal of Polar Depths, then levels into Guo Jia and Fabled Sapphire Fatestone. Seaside Ringleader is lost to the level-up banish; the early mills hit Fractal of Rain for Dit and Windmill Engineer for boeboe.

boeboe has a clunky opener (three Dungeon Guides and little other Wind). They play Angelic Channeling before levelling, imbue a Windmill Engineer to show a Reclaim, and bank Fatestone of Heaven cards under Channeling for later.

boeboe levels Guo Jia quickly using Dungeon Guide banishes for quest counters, flips Seiryuu first (ten counters versus Genbu's nine), and sends an Arcane Blast to their banishment off the attack. A short judge ruling checks how Angelic Channeling's top/bottom trigger resolves.

Dit develops Frostsworn Paladins and holds defensive interaction. When Seiryuu attacks a Paladin, Dit sacrifices that defending Paladin to Primordial Ritual. The dragon's on-attack trigger still resolves.

boeboe plays Optical Control naming action cards, so Dit's Fugue costs four more. Auspicious Manifestation banishes Seiryuu so it returns awake at end of turn and can taunt. The line buys time but cannot beat the mill-out plan.

Dit presents a third Fractal of Polar Depths, and boeboe concedes to the mill-out line. The casters explain a self, self, opponent sequence and discuss naming Fantasia with Optical Control as an alternative.

games.summary: boeboe wins with a sideboarded lock and Arcane Blast

beats.text: boeboe opens with an imbued Benediction Angel and Dream Fairies. The fairies stop Dit from playing Bullfrog or Frostsworn Paladin for most of the game.
Nullifying Lantern hits the board. All cards in graveyards become no element, so Dit's Polar Depths mill and Deluge turn off. Dit holds Unbroken Mustang to remove it.
Dit draws a second Unbroken Mustang but puts one into memory to play the other. Stifling Trap stops that Mustang’s trigger, leaving Nullifying Lantern intact; Dit has no Primordial Ritual response.

Boeboe adds Censer of Restful Peace, which Dit removes with Fracturize, then uses Purifying Thurible. The second Mustang is delayed; Dit later uses Enfeebling Orb before committing it. Boeboe retains Psychopomp's Gale as graveyard interaction and develops Aella, Zephyr's Hand, repeatedly suppressing Forest Cake for cards.
Dit stays alive with Song of Frost, Enfeebling Orb, Spalling Cleanse and Beastbond Boots, flips Genbu, and tries to dodge the dragon. The round timer runs low as boeboe stays patient.

Dit negates the first dragon attack trigger with Song of Frost. boeboe uses Byakko's Command to wake the dragon so it attacks again, and then fires the stored Arcane Blast for 11 damage that Dit cannot stop.

games.summary: Dit wins — game loss to boeboe for an illegal deck

beats.text: As the players prepare game three near the end of the round, boeboe accidentally shuffles a generated Arcane Blast into the deck and immediately calls a judge. The casters report a game loss for presenting an illegal deck, giving Dit the match 2-1.

matches.round: Round 2 (Day 1) — Suited debuts against Astra Arisanna

players.name: TlsoVotl
players.deck: Fire Suited (Proxy Vault Duchess's Thorns, Fiery Interference)

players.name: Aqua
players.deck: Wind Astra Arisanna (Polaris, Cosmic Bolt glimpse)

sideboardNotes.text: TlsoVotl is expected to bring in Infernal Vessel and Safeguard Amulet (the casters doubt Nullifying Mirror makes it, as Aqua does not imbue). In the post-match interview, TlsoVotl also names Pseudo Trickery and Mortal Ambition as side tech against champion-cleave decks such as Lorraine.
Aqua is expected to bring in extra Imperial Countermeasure and Regenerate for more healing. Aqua is on the play for game 2 because they chose after losing game 1.

games.summary: TlsoVotl wins on card advantage and a clutch Fiery Interference

beats.text: TlsoVotl wins the roll and opens with Four of Spades. Suited cards replace themselves via Cardistry, so TlsoVotl keeps eight or more cards in influence and rebuilds the board quickly after Aqua's sweeps.

Aqua develops Polaris and uses herb sacrifices to build its counters. Calming Breeze checks the early attacks while the board wipe forces TlsoVotl to rebuild. Aqua later reaches Astra and starts looking for Cosmic Bolt.
TlsoVotl lands Arthur, Young Heir and The Duchess to pressure Aqua's Arisanna. Aqua answers Arthur with Cosmic Bolt after using Three Visits for healing.
TlsoVotl uses Peppered Chef on The Duchess to push damage through Calming Breeze, then Fiery Interference stops Aqua's Serene Spirit heal and closes the game.

games.summary: Aqua wins with defensive cards and Cosmic Bolts

beats.text: Aqua starts with two Calming Breezes, two Gentle Beseeches and Gentle Respite. TlsoVotl's hand has few cheap allies and uses Backup Charger to fix it.

TlsoVotl develops Three of Hearts and Rouge, then hard-activates Eight of Hearts after Polaris clears the board. A later Meteor Strike is met by Three of Spades protecting Eight of Hearts. TlsoVotl, rather than Aqua, materializes Safeguard Amulet.

Imperial Countermeasure and Calming Breeze keep Aqua alive. Horde Counter stops TlsoVotl’s later Verita attempt after Eight of Hearts sacrifices allies. Aqua’s Astra Sight finds Meteor Strike, and the growing Cosmic Bolt damage closes the game.

games.summary: TlsoVotl wins in overtime with Verita and Arthur

beats.text: TlsoVotl goes first and opens Four of Hearts into Arthur, Young Heir on turn two. Aqua has no Arisanna on turn one, so Polaris is two turns away.

Aqua uses Angelic Channeling to put Meteor Strike on top. After a Dungeon Guide level up, Aqua wipes the board with Meteor Strike via Cosmic Astroscope, and Polaris with Calming Breeze and Stifling Gyre blunt the follow-up.

TlsoVotl rebuilds with Verita by banishing suited cards with a combined cost of ten, followed by The Duchess. Aqua uses two Imperial Countermeasures but reaches 20 damage, and the match enters overtime.

TlsoVotl sequences Arthur's swing first, then attacks with Verita and the others. Aqua has only a Cosmic Bolt to answer the board and is one glimpse short of stabilizing. TlsoVotl takes the match 2-1.

players.name: Noel
players.deck: Water Exia Jin (Chess Club build: Huaji of Abyssal Fall, Sunce, Looking Glass)

players.name: Tress
players.deck: Water Exia Jin (Regal mill-out build: four Regals, Dynastic Whirlpool side)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters recommend Dynastic Whirlpool and Viridian Protective Trinket for Tress. Dynastic Whirlpool is played twice in game two; a complete swap list is not shown.

The casters recommend the fourth Regal Inquisition, Engulf and Crimson Rupture for Noel. They note that Noel’s registered list has no Dynastic Whirlpool or anti-mill reset; these are sideboard recommendations rather than confirmed counts.

games.summary: Tress wins — survives Noel’s final attack to complete the mill-out

beats.text: Both players start the long Jin mirror with Spirit of Serene Water. Noel uses Gentle Respite and Back-up Charger well and uses Dungeon Guide to hit Jin level three first.
Noel plays Regal Inquisition to strip Tress's hand, leaving only Angel cards. Tress answers with Angelic Channeling, Fractal of Waves and Quicksilver Grail to rebuild.

Noel’s Seething Intercession finds Return to the Archive. Tress’s separate Seething Intercession finds Enrage, Engulf and Regal Inquisition, giving Tress useful cards protected from discard while banished.
Tress sets up Shade-Mist Priestess (recover one on every damage) and keeps a Regal in banishment. With four Regals, Tress changes the plan to a mill-out, and Noel has no anti-mill tech.

Noel transforms Huaji into Huaji of Abyssal Fall and adds Sun Ce, who restores durability. The weapon can deal unpreventable damage to its own attacker to increase attack damage; the casters correct themselves that Sun Ce cannot survive that self-damage. Noel later uses Relentless Outburst, while Shademist Priestess’s triggers soften the damage to Tress.
Noel has drawn through the library and makes a final damage push. After earlier Mend Flesh recovery, Tress shows Regenerate to survive the closing turn and win game one.

games.summary: Noel wins — Tress runs out of healing, tying the match 1–1

beats.text: Both players play more carefully: Noel holds Backup Charger for a level up, and Tress plays Topsy Decree to deny Noel's float. The two sides trade Angelic Channeling and Fractal Fracturize tricks to set up top-of-deck cards.
Tress uses Dynastic Whirlpool to mill the cards Noel put on top with Channeling: three Regals and two Engulfs go to the graveyard. This removes Noel's protection and the main way to mill Tress.

Noel switches to a damage plan. Shuangji, Berserker Plate, Fracturize and an Enrage push huge swings, and Tress answers with Crimson Rupture on the Shuangji plus Pearled Prayer, Regenerate and Serene Spirit.
Tress digs for a heal using Tome of Abyssal Heaven but cannot find a second one. Noel wins game two with damage, tying the match 1–1 as time expires. The casters praise Noel for playing to outs.

matches.round: Round 4 (Day 1) — Fractals Diao Chan against Genbu

players.name: TeamTrueCaban
players.deck: Water Fractals Diao Chan (influence-denial build: four Fractal of Intrusion, Acquiescing Rejection, Topsy Decree)

matches.result: Draw — 1-1 in games, game 3 drawn at time

sideboardNotes.text: The casters predict Caban brings in Crystalline Mirror (to remove Safeguard Amulet), Expel the Departed against Polar Depths, Song of Frost and perhaps Delusional Vapors. These are caster predictions, not a confirmed list.
The casters discuss Beastbond Boots, Expel the Departed, Engulf and Regal Inquisition for Superior. Boots appears and Engulf is played in game two; Expel is milled rather than shown stopping a play.

games.summary: Caban wins — influence denial and a Burst Asunder that Superior cannot stop

beats.text: Caban plays a Fractals list that mostly runs Fractal of Intrusion, Acquiescing Rejection and four Topsy Decrees, so Superior's float and memory are banished each turn. The goal is to keep Superior's influence too low to flip Genbu.

Superior starts with imbued Fractal of Rain, then Safeguard Amulet and Tidestone Bovine. Early mills lose Fractal of Polar Depths rather than putting it in hand, making the mill-out route harder to assemble.

Caban Fracturizes cards to add fractals, uses Refracting Missile to pull out Safeguard Amulet, and negates every important play with Glimmering Refusal and Acquiescing Rejection. Superior's Diamond Ribbon gives influence but cannot get a play through.

beats.text: With only nine minutes left, both players have to race. Superior's Shademist Priestess recovers damage, and Caban Fracturizes the Safeguard Amulet and builds fractals.

Superior removes Nullifying Lantern with Unbroken Mustang and continues developing Tidestone Bovine, Throne-keeper Bullfrog and Diamond Ribbon. Both players have Enfeebling Orb available as they wait for an opening.

Superior flips Genbu, reaches Guo Jia level three and activates Genbu. TLux responds with Psychopomp’s Gale; Superior uses Tidal Lock, and TLux activates Enfeebling Orb before Superior follows with Engulf. Gale is negated. Superior’s own Orb pressures TLux’s hand, and Veiling Breeze prevents only four before the 27-damage finishing attack. Superior reaches 8-0-4.

games.summary: ChemCollapse wins — Regal Inquisition clears Song of Frost, then Seiryuu's Command

beats.text: ChemCollapse goes first and turbos: Forest Cake, then Angelic Channeling banishing three advanced-element cards for three quest counters. Guo Jia reaches level three on the third turn.

mDuo13 uses Throne-Keeper Bullfrog to hold off attacks, plays Fractal of Polar Depths and taxes ChemCollapse’s Dungeon Guide with Cerulean Decree. Later, Fabled Sapphire Fatestone mills mDuo13’s Bullfrog and ChemCollapse’s Tricastles of Lucenia, denying ChemCollapse a powerful draw.

ChemCollapse delays transforming Seiryuu and uses Aella to target mDuo13’s Bullfrog; mDuo13 responds with Primordial Ritual. Later, Regal Inquisition discards both Songs of Frost from mDuo13’s hand. The replacement draws find neither another Song nor an answer to Seiryuu’s Command, which wins the game.

games.summary: ChemCollapse wins — Sasha shuts off the graveyard and Uther removes Genbu

beats.text: mDuo13 develops Tidestone Bovine and Fractal of Rain, while ChemCollapse uses Purifying Thurible to remove floating memory. Genbu eventually transforms. The casters explore several possible lethal lines, but mDuo13 instead takes a nine-damage Resonating Fugue line.

ChemCollapse plays Censer of Restful Peace, then Uther, Illustrious King banishes Genbu while mDuo13’s Guo Jia is still level one. Uther later intercepts Tidestone Bovine and defeats it in retaliation.

ChemCollapse develops Sasha, Purifying Acolyte and Smoke Bombs. Sasha fosters, banishing the graveyards and preventing cards from entering them while its effect remains active. Aella adds another protective option, and mDuo13 concedes.

sideboardNotes.text: Yadon has Smoke Out main and in the side (to deal with Cheshire Cat), Planted Explosive ×2 and Crystallized Destiny. He says in the interview that he plays one Smoke Out main for turns where he has no preparation counter.
The casters expect additional Snow White, Weiss Queen and discuss increasing Rude from three main-deck copies to four. These are boarding predictions, not confirmed changes.

games.summary: Fallinbuu14 wins — Krustallan Archer and Ranger Strides for 12 through the Serene Spirit

beats.text: Fallinbuu14 has no distant enabler in the opener and plays Aetheric Calibration, Inert Sword and Cheshire Cat (a 3/3 with stealth and spell shroud) instead. Yadon uses Incapacitate on Reposition and Planted Explosive on the Cat.

Yadon opens with Angelic Channeling to protect Luxem Sight, Uncover the Plot and Lightweaver's Assault, levels to Zander, Deft Executor and then uses Dungeon Guide to reach Blinding Steel, and stabilizes with Blinding Steel reveals and Tariff Ring.

Fallinbuu14 develops two Frostsworn Paladins, Quickstep Treads and Weaving Manastream, and Frostbind stops Planted Explosive aimed at a Paladin. A later Incapacitate prevents Diana from becoming distant. Krustallan Archer still attacks with floating memory and the bonuses from Ranger Strides and Cheshire Cat, producing the twelve-damage finish through Spirit of Serene Fire.

games.summary: Yadon wins — Exploit Vulnerability sets up a lethal Lightweaver’s Assault

beats.text: Fallinbuu14 struggles to build pressure despite finding distant enablers. Yadon’s imbued Topsy Decree strips floating memory, and Zander reaches Blinding Steel with zero damage. Charge the Soul is initially held; later Calibration misses compound Fallinbuu14’s resource problems.

Yadon initially finds Lightweaver’s Assault and Sadi, then eventually Gleaming Cut; no Luxem Sight appears in this game. Fallinbuu14 Fracturizes Insignia of the Corhazi and uses Palvor Sword to remove Sadi and banish Yadon’s graveyard, rebuilding with another Frostsworn Paladin. Resolute Stand buys Yadon another turn.

The casters first propose playing two Lightweaver’s Assaults through Flash Grenade. Yadon instead uses Exploit Vulnerability, then activates one Assault while putting the other into memory. The reveal trigger and the activated Assault supply lethal damage. The casters infer that this line also leaves Incapacitate available; it is not played.

games.summary: Yadon wins — a final Lightweaver's Assault, with Fallinbuu14 two damage short

beats.text: Fallinbuu14 misses with Aetheric Calibration, finding Frostbind and Backsteps instead of a charge. Yadon removes Frostsworn Paladin with Planted Explosive and uses an imbued Topsy Decree to remove floating memory and discard Take Aim. A later Cheshire Cat is also removed by Planted Explosive.

Yadon channels Luxem Sight, Gleaming Cut and Excalibur, then reaches Blinding Steel; the casters note a missed Lost Providence trigger. Fallinbuu14 resolves Take Aim through Incapacitate with Frostbind and commits Ranger Strides to an eleven-damage Diana attack with a twelve-card glimpse. Chalice of Blood helps Yadon draw the stacked cards. A main-phase Topsy Decree removes Weaving Manastream, and Spirit of Serene Fire and Tariff Ring help Yadon survive.

Fallinbuu14 gets within three, then two, damage of lethal on consecutive turns. Yadon uses Exploit Vulnerability and Mercenary's Blade on the Paladin, and finishes with Sadi and Lightweaver's Assault revealing seven cards.

games.summary: Zetdivx wins — Diana pressure races Stevo before Jin level three

beats.text: Zetdivx opens with Backstep to become distant, materializes Diana and Aquamirage Whisper, then loads Refreshing Charge. The first attack sets up the next draws. Stevo starts on Spirit of Fortuitous Water and develops slowly.
Frostsworn Paladin and Krustallan Archer add damage each turn, and Stevo does not get to level three. Stevo's Jin is at 20 total life and cannot heal out of Zetdivx's damage.

Frostsworn Paladin pushes Jin toward 19 damage, and the casters identify Charge the Soul as the final point before Zetdivx takes game one. They count 14 damage on the finishing turn, before Jin reaches level three.

games.summary: Zetdivx wins — floating-memory denial stalls Jin, then Tactical Retreat stops the heal

beats.text: Stevo switches to Spirit of Serene Water and opens Gentle Respite. Enchanted Fete heals and draws into memory before Jin reaches level two. Stevo then uses Fracturize on Quickstep Treads, but its on-enter draw still resolves.

Zetdivx uses Aetheric Reforging to banish the Fracturize floating memory Stevo needs for the next level. With a hand full of Exia cards, Stevo has to materialize Backup Charger instead. Krustallan Archer and Frostsworn Paladin keep attacking.

After Inert Sword and Reposition, Zetdivx answers the Serene Water heal during combat with Tactical Retreat, ending that combat before the heal resolves. Diana and Cheshire Cat then finish Jin at level two. Zetdivx advances to the semifinals and secures a Worlds invitation.

sideboardNotes.text: The casters consider Turbo Charge, Blessed Clergy, Topsy Decree and Mystic Purifier for Jett. Turbo Charge is confirmed in game two. In the interview, Jett says he has not sided in Blessed Clergy during the event.

The casters expect another Tricastles of Lucenia and discuss Blanche, Topsy Decree, Scatter Essence and Sasha as options for ChemCollapse. Blanche is identified in the game-three hand; the complete boarding package is not shown.

games.summary: ChemCollapse wins — Tricastles of Lucenia locks Razorgale, then Seiryuu's Command

beats.text: ChemCollapse uses Beseech the Winds to reach Guo Jia level one on the first turn, then develops quest counters with Portentous Tanggu and Scout the Land. Jett builds influence with Backup Charger and repeated Fluffy Shopkeep plays.

After Dungeon Guide takes Guo Jia to level three, ChemCollapse plays Tricastles of Lucenia, preventing non-advanced element card activations. Once per turn, any player may banish a norm or advanced element card from hand to make Tricastles lose all abilities until end of turn.

ChemCollapse develops Uther to banish Razorgale Calling, then Aella and Royal Oathguard. Aella suppresses Essence Crucible when Jett tries to disable Tricastles. Jett commits three Dream Fairies to the opposing allies, eventually freeing Razorgale, but falls below the hand size needed for Ensnaring Fumes.
ChemCollapse flips Seiryuu, plays Seiryuu's Command (triple on-enter) to generate an Arcane Blast and empower it by eight. The Blast costs nothing and finishes Jett.

games.summary: Jett wins — Aesan Protector chip damage, then Zephyr and Veiling Breeze on the last Razorgale trigger

beats.text: Jett brings in Turbo Charge, plays Windmill Engineer and Aesan Protector early, and wants a board that can kill Tricastles of Lucenia in two turns. Fairy Whispers finds Razorgale Calling.

ChemCollapse uses Beseech the Winds to level, losing a Tricastles of Lucenia to the level-up banish, and later draws with Incandescent Reliquary. ChemCollapse’s Purifying Thurible removes cards from Jett’s graveyard. ChemCollapse plays Regal Inquisition on Jett, discarding Ensnaring Fumes, but Jett draws another copy immediately, keeping Seiryuu constrained.

Jett develops two Razorgales and Essence Crucible, brewing two Distilled Waters. ChemCollapse uses two Imperial Countermeasures to absorb damage while Aesan Protector keeps applying pressure. In response to Ducal Seal, Jett Zephyrs his own Protector and follows with Veiling Breeze for the final Razorgale triggers.

games.summary: Jett wins the deciding game (not shown in full)

beats.text: ChemCollapse goes first for the first time in the match, uses Beseech the Winds on turn one and Portentous Tanggu, and holds Blanch and Dungeon Guide. Jett opens with Windmill Engineer, Aesan Protector and Fluffy Shopkeep, to keep at least four damage of allies on board against another Tricastle.

Jett finds Razorgale Calling, Aesan Protector and Ensnaring Fumes with Fairy Whispers and keeps six cards in hand so the dragon stays locked. The broadcast cuts to the semifinal and confirms Jett closed out the game 2-1 within the next couple of turns.

players.name: Zetdivx
players.deck: Water Aetherwing Diana (Apex build: two Aetherwings, Cheshire Cat, Ranger Strides, Take Aim ×2, Aetheric Reforging)

players.name: Jett
players.deck: Razorgale Arisanna (raccoon package: four Bandit, two Protector Raccoon; Essence Crucible, Aesan Protector)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters recommend Obscured Offering and discuss Topsy Decree, Blessed Clergy, Fluffy Shopkeep and Stifling Gyre for Jett. Turbo Charge and Fluffy Shopkeep are confirmed in game two; the complete boarding package is not shown.

The casters discuss another Aetheric Reforging, Nullifying Mirror, Nullifying Lantern and Shademist Priestess. Expel the Departed, two Reforgings and a nullifying regalia are identified in game two; Mirror and Priestess are confirmed in game three.

games.summary: Zetdivx wins — a patient build-up, then a 19-damage one-shot

beats.text: Zetdivx goes first as the top seed. Jett develops Censer of Restful Peace, and Zetdivx removes it with Fracturize. Jett’s Protector Raccoon removes the float before Zetdivx levels Diana. Aetheric Calibration then finds Aetheric Reforging to load Aquamirage Whisper.

Jett uses Protector Raccoon, Purifying Thurible and Veiling Breeze to blank the Whisper's first hit trigger. Jett has zero damage taken for much of the game and builds a hand of eight cards, while Zetdivx gets no float value.

Jett lands two Razorgales and Essence Crucible, but Zetdivx's Fracturize removes the Crucible (Jett has no Obscured Offering). Jett's hand has clunky norm cards, and Cyclical Breeze to get Veiling Breeze back is answered by Aetheric Reforging.

Zetdivx uses Flash Grenade to survive Jett’s attempted damage turn, then loads another Weaving Manastream while materializing Smoke Bombs. Two Take Aims and Ranger Strides go onto distant Diana, whose Aquamirage Whisper holds five charges. The nineteen-damage Diana attack wins; Quickstep Treads taxes Jett’s possible responses, and the Archer remains available as follow-up.

games.summary: Jett wins — board control with raccoons and Aesan Protector

beats.text: Zetdivx starts with a Krustallan Archer to bait Veiling Breeze and holds Expel the Departed, Fracturize and the second Reforging. But Jett's Aesan Protector, Bandit and Protector Raccoon block float, and Dream Fairy locks Cheshire Cat.

Jett repeatedly returns allies with Aesan Protector and Reclaim. Zetdivx uses Seeker’s Aetherwing to attack the Dream Fairy holding Cheshire Cat, but Jett’s Skirting Step prevents the damage. Charge the Soul had gone to Jett’s champion, leaving Fairy healthy enough to survive that line.

Jett builds a large hand and an attacking board, then develops Tariff Ring and Razorgale Calling. Zetdivx Expels the first Calling; Jett finds another with Scout the Land. With Tariff Ring taxing attacks and Jett still controlling the graveyard, Zetdivx concedes.

games.summary: Jett wins — Essence Crucible with three counters and double Razorgale

beats.text: Jett’s opening Bandit finds another Bandit on the sixth scavenge card and repeatedly removes Zetdivx’s floating memory. Zetdivx builds influence with Backup Charger and plays Shademist Priestess, forcing Jett to find an answer before Razorgale damage can accumulate efficiently.

Zetdivx uses Drown in Aether on a rested Bandit, later Frostbinds Reclaim to secure an attack, and trades Weaving Manastream plus Krustallan Archer for Aesan Protector. Ranger Strides, Inert Sword, Quickstep Treads and Nullifying Mirror build a threatening board. A later Drown in Aether removes the attacking Dream Fairy and frees Priestess; Jett’s Viridian Protective Trinket makes it cost four.

Jett brews a speed potion and two Distilled Waters, bringing Essence Crucible to three counters. Fairy Whispers finds a second Razorgale, so each wind activation threatens eight damage. The casters discuss responding above the Priestesses’ recovery triggers, but correct their lethal calculation when recovery resolves during Scout the Land. A following Fairy Whispers supplies the finishing triggers.

players.deck: Water Aetherwing Diana (Apex build: Cheshire Cat, Krustallan Archer, Seeker's Aetherwing, Aetheric Reforging, Nullifying Mirror)

players.name: Jett
players.deck: Razorgale Arisanna (raccoon package, Essence Crucible, Viridian Protective Trinket, Tariff Ring)

matches.result: Jett wins 2-1 and is the North American Nationals 2026 champion

sideboardNotes.text: The casters recommend Expel the Departed, Aetheric Reforging, Nullifying Mirror and Shademist Priestess for Quarax. Mirror appears in game two; Priestess and Expel are seen in game three, when Expel removes Razorgale Calling.

The casters suggest Obscured Offering and another Zephyr, with Fluffy Shopkeep and Stifling Gyre as possibilities. Topsy Decree is later identified in Jett’s game-two hand; the full boarding package is not confirmed.

games.summary: Jett wins — Purifying Thurible and Protector Raccoon deny the float, then two Razorgales

beats.text: Jett opens with Purifying Thurible (not Censer of Restful Peace) and holds Protector Raccoon. Quarax's Krustallan Archer attack is answered by Protector Raccoon banishing the Charge the Soul float, so no card is drawn. Jett waits for the last moment to respond.

Bandit scavenges into a third raccoon. Fluffy Shopkeep, an animal, is protected by Protector Raccoon, and Viridian Protective Trinket makes Quarax's water cards cost two more. Quarax's Cheshire Cat kills the Fluffy Shopkeep and the Raccoon.

Jett plays two Razorgales and brews a Speed Potion in Essence Crucible. Quarax's Fracturize removes the Crucible (Jett has no Obscured Offering). Dream Fairy kills the Cheshire Cat, and Aesan Protector returns it to hand. Razorgale pings, Cyclical Breeze and Tariff Ring leave Quarax with one damage from death.

Quarax develops Flash Grenade but must first become distant to use it. Jett activates Tariff Ring and answers Diana’s attack with Calming Breeze, preventing the attack damage while adding Razorgale triggers. Quarax is left one damage from defeat and concedes.

games.summary: Quarax wins — Krustallan Archer with a float and Jett cannot imbue Skirting Step

beats.text: Quarax goes first, then uses Backstep to set up Diana and Aquamirage Whisper. Jett’s Calming Breeze stops the opening shot. Nullifying Mirror later removes Veiling Breeze as a useful defensive option while Quarax builds pressure.

Jett plays Purifying Thurible and a Protector Raccoon, but Quarax Fracturizes the Thurible to force the response. Bandit scavenges six cards and puts two Razorgales and a Dream Fairy at the bottom, which hurts Jett's win conditions.

Quarax attacks with Diana, finds floating memory and follows with Krustallan Archer. Jett plays Skirting Step without imbuing it. The casters initially calculate that it saves him at one life and discuss leveling, then correct themselves: the damage prevention also requires imbue. With Topsy Decree among Jett’s cards preventing that imbue, the Archer attack ends game two.

games.summary: Jett wins — Bandit, Protector Raccoon and Razorgale's pings close out the title

beats.text: Jett opens with Windmill Engineer and then Censer of Restful Peace, holding Bandits while Quarax builds influence. When Bandit is finally activated, Quarax plays Frozen Dismissal; Jett pays four and finds Protector Raccoon on the fifth scavenge card. Quarax loses Tactical Retreat on leveling and has no distant enabler available for Diana’s on-enter, leaving her without an Aetherwing.

Jett levels to Arisanna with Reclaim and Windmill Engineer, imbues Skirting Step, and plays Razorgale Calling and Dream Fairy on the Cheshire Cat. Quarax finds Seeker's Aetherwing and Prudent Nock, but cannot get damage through the reclaimed Windmill Engineers and Dream Fairy.

Jett develops Essence Crucible and brews a potion. Quarax’s Expel the Departed removes Razorgale Calling, but Cyclical Breeze retrieves it without a Reforging response. The replayed Calling and Aesan Protector bring Quarax within two damage of defeat. Jett waits until Quarax attempts Reposition, then plays Veiling Breeze; the Razorgale trigger deals lethal damage and wins the title.
